newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon may sell, merge appliance group.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon may sell, merge appliance group.

text.p: Raytheon Co. said Sunday it is evaluating alternatives for its appliance group, and may consider selling or merging the division.

The appliance unit, which had revenues of about $1.5 billion in 1996, is involved in major home appliances, commercial laundry equipment, heating and air conditioning, commercial cooking and electronic controls under the Amana, Speed Queen, UniMac and Huebsch brand names.
It has about 8,000 employees worldwide, with facilities in Iowa, Wisconsin, Tennessee, South Carolina, Arkansas, Kentucky and Florida, as well as Germany and Spain.

The potential sale or merger of the division follows Raytheon's plans to acquire Texas Instruments Inc.'s defence electronics unit for $2.95 billion and General Motors Corp.s Hughes Aircraft for $9.5 billion.
The company said it has retained Credit Suisse First Boston as an adviser to assist with the evaluation.

Raytheon said in a statement that it was assessing the group "in the context of Raytheon's financial priorities and the belief that the appliance group may have greater value to another company with more focus on the markets served by the group."
"We can't specify what the timetable will be" for disposition of the appliance group, Raytheon spokesman Robert McWade said.
However, he said the move would be in keeping with Raytheon's decision to focus on its core businesses, such as commercial and defence electronics, engineering and construction, and aviation.
